discovery_articles.title: Gloucester Sea Serpent Statue in Gloucester, Massachusetts
discovery_articles.snippet: It's a beautiful summer day in a quiet seaside community. People are flocking to the water to enjoy the ocean breeze, splashing waves, shining sun, and the sound of gulls. However, beneath the waters, something monstrous lurks.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: For over two centuries, the waters off Gloucester hosted so many credible sea serpent sightings that the Linnaean Society of New England launched a formal scientific investigation in 1817 — complete with sworn affidavits from dozens of witnesses. The monster was respectable enough to earn a Latin name before anyone decided, quietly, to stop looking.

discovery_articles.title: Astronomers Peered at the Early Universe and May Have Discovered a New Kind of Celestial Object: Black Hole Stars
discovery_articles.snippet: Since the James Webb Space Telescope started collecting data in 2022, it has found puzzling objects dubbed little red dots. A new study suggests they might be giant black holes with some characteristics of stars
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The 'little red dots' spotted by the James Webb Space Telescope may be objects that shouldn't exist by our current understanding of physics — black holes so enormous they've essentially grown a stellar skin around themselves. If confirmed, they wouldn't just be a new discovery; they'd be a new category of existence.

garden_note.note: August evenings in Zürich carry that particular late-summer warmth — the kind that lingers in the stone walls and the heavy heads of sunflowers long after the light fades.
